_note: Batch 2 — HVAC / home-services rollups. Imported via import-to-airtable.mjs. Businesses import as review_status=pending; spot-check in Airtable, then flip to verified. Ownership-focused batch: HVAC has far less firm-specific regulatory/litigation paper than veterinary, so only Alpine (Apex) and Goldman Sachs (Sila) carry defensible Tier B tags; Wrench, ARS, and TurnPoint are ownership-only. The 2011 Arizona AG action against ARS was deliberately NOT attached to GI Partners — it was business-level conduct under prior ownership (pre-2020). Reused firms already in the base (TSG Consumer Partners, Oak Hill, Partners Group) are co-owners noted in platform_company but the owning_firm_id points to each platform's lead/majority sponsor. National chains have no locations enumerated (deferred; map view out of v1 scope).

firms.notes: Majority owner of Wrench Group (HVAC/plumbing/electrical) since 2019; TSG Consumer Partners and Oak Hill Capital took a minority stake in Nov 2022.
Founder and lead sponsor of Apex Service Partners (est. 2019), the largest US residential HVAC/plumbing/electrical platform.

tags.description: Oct 2023 ~$3.4B single-asset continuation-fund transaction for Apex — among the largest in PE history — let Alpine return capital to investors while retaining the asset; in May 2026 Apollo Funds took a ~$2B minority stake at a $10B valuation, capitalizing the rollup further.

firms.notes: Goldman Sachs Alternatives (the firm's private-equity business). Acquired Sila Services in early 2025.

tags.description: Acquired Sila Services from Morgan Stanley Capital Partners in early 2025 in a roughly $1.5B sponsor-to-sponsor deal including debt — a leveraged continuation of the HVAC roll-up.

In Sept 2025 the Nexstar Network — the largest plumbing/HVAC trade group — severed ties with all PE-backed members (~1/3 of its 800 members) over the roll-up model; Forbes cited Sila's 28-acquisition consolidation as a leading example of the consolidation the group rejected.

firms.notes: Made a majority investment in ARS / American Residential Services in 2020; Charlesbank Capital Partners remains a co-owner.
Private-equity arm of the Canadian pension OMERS. Acquired TurnPoint Services from Trivest Partners in late 2020.
